finding.claim: OS command injection: the unauthenticated /ping endpoint concatenates the req.query.host query parameter into a shell command string run via exec(), so shell metacharacters (; | $() backticks) give arbitrary command execution as the server user.
finding.sink: child_process.exec (spawns /bin/sh -c) at tools.js:7, with command output returned to the caller at tools.js:11

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping with no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated directly into the string 'ping -c 1 ' + host and passed to exec()
stdout is returned in the response, so injected command output is exfiltrated (e.g. host=127.0.0.1;id)

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist or hostname/IP regex. No authentication or authorization middleware (only express app, no app.use). Not using execFile with an args array. A non-string value (array from host[]=) is also unchecked. The error branch returns 502 but only after execution. No other controls exist in the repo.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host straight to exec() (shell) with no validation or auth middleware on the route at tools.js:6, and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so an anonymous caller gets command execution with output.

verdict_facts.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (shell) with no auth, validation or allowlist, and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so an anonymous caller can inject commands like host=127.0.0.1;id and read the output (tools.js:6-13; tools.js is the only file).
